text:
kenji: Hey — terraform apply hitting a lock in prod s3 backend, keeps failing with 'Another state operation is in progress' when trying to apply LB changes. Anyone saw this today?
sophie: saw a blip earlier, we had a failed deploy from CI. Link: https://ci.internal/1234 :grimacing:
alex: error message? can you paste the `terraform apply` output?
kenji: stack: terraform v1.5.6, backend s3://redwood-tf-prod, dynamodb table redwood-tf-locks
kenji: the error: 
```
Error: Error locking state: ConditionalCheckFailedException: The conditional request failed
	status code: 400, request id: abc-123

Another state operation is in progress.
```
maria: that's the dynamodb lease hitting the conditional check. Usually means old lock wasn't cleaned up (CI runner crashed).
jules: 2 quick options: 1) inspect the lock item in the DynamoDB table and confirm which locker holds it, or 2) if you know no one is running, `terraform force-unlock` with the ID.
kenji: can someone remind me the CLI to inspect the item? don't want to nuke if CI is still running.
sophie: `aws dynamodb get-item --table-name redwood-tf-locks --key '{"LockID":{"S":"<LOCK-ID>"}}' --region us-west-2` should show the holder + info. also check S3 for the lock file `terraform.tfstate` and the state lock key.
alex: CI runners use locker id like `ci-runner/<job-id>`. Check CloudWatch logs for the job id in the timestamp range.
kenji: ran get-item, found: `Holder: ci-runner/2456`, `Info: apply failed`, TTL expired 2m ago. So CI probably crashed and lock stuck.
jules: safe to run `terraform force-unlock <LOCK-ID>` if you're sure no other apply is active. After unlock, run `terraform plan -refresh=true` to pick up drift.
maria: FYI you can also use `terraform plan -refresh=false` to avoid long refresh if you just want to re-run apply quickly, but that risks missing drift. for infra changes touching LB you probably want refresh.
kenji: before force-unlock: should we `terraform state pull` or `terraform refresh -target=module.lb`?
sophie: `terraform state pull` is safe — gives you the raw state to inspect. `terraform refresh -target` will make remote calls and update state; do it if you suspect resource drift.
alex: if the apply previously partially created resources, consider `terraform import` for missing resources. example: `terraform import module.foo.aws_lb.this arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:1234:loadbalancer/app/my-lb/abcd`
maria: and if a resource is known-bad, `terraform taint module.foo.aws_instance.bar` then run plan/apply to recreate.
kenji: I'll coordinate with CI to ensure no jobs running, then force-unlock and run `terraform plan -refresh=true -var-file=prod.tfvars`. tagging @ops-bot to post a short maintenance note to #incidents if we need to roll back.
ops-bot: NOTE: Scheduled quick maintenance window (internal) — kenji will attempt to clear terraform state lock in 10m.
jules: ping me before `apply` so I can watch logs and abort if something weird.
kenji: thanks all — will report back after unlock + plan.
(10m later)
kenji: unlocked with `terraform force-unlock 01F...`, ran `terraform plan -refresh=true` and plan looks good. No unexpected deletes. proceeding to apply now.
sophie: nice. monitoring dashboards for LB health in case of flapping. :thumbsup:
alex: if apply errors again, capture `terraform apply -auto-approve -lock=false` output and we'll triage; but avoid `-lock=false` in prod unless coordinated.
kenji: apply finished ✅. No drift and LB health steady. Closing thread.
